text.p: UK mobile telephone company Orange Plc said on Monday that its total subscribers more than doubled during 1996 to over 785,000 from 379,000 at the end of 1995.
The company said it added 125,000 net new subscribers in the fourth quarter of 1996, the highest quarterly connections ever achieved by Orange.
Orange said it now had an 11.5 percent share of the total UK market, against seven percent at the end of 1995. Over 1996, it captured 29 percent of net market growth.

The company said its "churn" or disconnection rate of 18.6 percent in 1996 remained significantly lower than the industry average. It said it had boosted coverage to 92 percent from 85 percent of the UK population.
Orange's Talkshare product, allowing two customers to share one subscription, has more than 20,000 subscribers following its launch during the last quarter.
"We stay right on our plan for growth of subscribers, market share, usage, network coverage and churn," said managing director Hans Snook.
"We look forward in 1997 to continuing to move ahead and to extending our international service through new roaming agreements and the introduction of dual band handsets."
